MyGov ATTENDANCE & WORK PROTOCOLS

1. Objective
To establish a transparent linkage between attendance inputs and payroll.
2. Scope
The policy is applicable to all resources of MyGov.
3. Work Protocol
a) All employees are required to work 8.5 hours a day including a 30-minute break
for lunch. Work timing schedule may vary from time to time based on business
requirements as specified by the organization from time to time. Employees may
be required to work a dditional hours during the work week / weekly offs, if
required, to fulfil the responsibility of a role/project and at the demand of work
exigencies. No additional compensation is payable for such stretched working
hours.
b) Employees attending office less than 4 hours in a day are required to mark half
day leave for that particular day.
4. Attendance:
a) All employees are expected to Mark-In & Mark-Out their attendance in biometric
machine installed in MeitY premises on daily basis. It is the responsibility of the
employee to ensure that their attendance is recorded in time.
b) If, in case of unforeseen circumstances, the resource is not able to report on
time, she/he should inform the manager of the same.
c) If due to any reason, employee misses registering their attendance through
biometrics, the attendance for the same should be shared with reporting manager
and HR on e-mail.
d) If the employee has a planned meeting (out of office) on any day and will not
be able to mark the attendance, the same should be shared with the reporting
manager and HR on e -mail. Mark-In & Mark -Out is to be marked in biometric
machine once the employee resumes office post meeting.

f) The attendance inputs are linked to payroll. If these inputs are at variance with
the real / physical attendance these will be treated as unauthentic data.
g) Unauthentic inputs are akin to dishonest conduct for a pecuniary advantage
and can result in disciplinary action.
5. Attendance Infractions
a) Attendance delinquencies will result in progressive disciplinary action up to
and including termination based on the following point system:
First Instance: A warning letter (via e-mail or postal mail) and a managerial
counselling session that will be documented and filed in the employee’s
personal records in the first instance of unauthorised absence;

Second Instance: A second case of unauthorised absence will entail a
warning letter (via e -mail or postal mail) to the absentee. 2 written
warnings within a span of 6 months, at any gap that is warranted, will invite
disciplinary action that may include, but will not be limited to, loss of pay,
adverse appraisal ratings, being relieved of responsibilities and suspension
from work for a period of time determined by competent authority; and

Third Instance: Termination. If three warning letters are issued then the
employee will be considered a habitual offender and services terminated. It
may be noted here that warning letters can be issued in quick succession
if, during a period of unauthorized absence, the employee fails to respond
to such letters.
b) If an employee is a no call - no show for three consecutive days it will be
considered a job abandonment, or termination without notice.

c) Employees may request exceptions for work absences from human
resources and management. These will be approved on a case -by-case
basis. If an employee is absent for three or more consecutive days on
medical grounds, evidence for excusing the absence, such as a doctor’s
note, prescriptions or reports, must be provided.

6. Exceptions/Modifications
Any exceptions to this policy would require prior approval.
The Policy may be modified / reviewed from time to time.
All exceptions/approvals are at the discretion of CEO, MyGov.

MyGov DOMESTIC TRAVEL POLICY

1. Applicability
All employees deputed at MyGov
2. General Principles
The following principles apply to business travel.
i. All business travels should be approved by the Head of Line of Business in
the format prescribed.
ii. All expenditure incurred while on tour should be within the entitlement
limits as defined in this Circular and in case of any deviation,
employees shall obtain a special approval from the Head of Line of
Business.

ii. Employees are encouraged to avail Super Saver, Apex or any other
schemes offered by various airlines, so as to incur the lowest expenditure.
iii. On receiving the travel approval from the Authorising Manager, the
resource can book the tickets as per entitlements
iv. Preference will be given to low-cost carriers where special rates have been
negotiated.
v. E Tickets and Boarding Passes must be retained and attached to the
reimbursement claim.
vi. Ticket issued for business trips shall remain the property of the
organisation.
vii. Exchange of tickets for cash or for tickets of a lower value is an
unacceptable conduct.
6. Other modes of travel:
Train Travel
i. Resources are entitled to 2nd A/C train travel while undertaking a business
Travel.
ii. Train travel is the preferred mode if the journey to a particular destination
is not scheduled to take more than 4 -6 hours or can be concluded

overnight. Air Travel is the preferred mode only in the event of non -
availability of train route.
Road Travel
i. A business travel can be undertaken by road where the distance between
home and business destination does not exceed 200 kms, road routes are
safe and travel time is short.
ii. Prior written approval for road travel would be required in line with the
approval matrix.
iii. The resource may choose to drive his own vehicle, in which case he / she
will be entitled to claim expenses @ Rs.10 per km.
iv. Journey made through three wheelers (Auto rickshaw), motor bike etc.,
for short distances, would be at the prescribed & prevailing rates of auto
rickshaw under that particular state/area.
v. Journey made within the city by Uber/ Ola would be reimbursed as per
actuals on submission of their receipt.
7. Stay Expenses:
i. Stay Expenses include all expenses billed by the Hotel or Guest House
except telephone calls and consumption or alcohol
ii. The reimbursement will be at actual expenditure (supported by bills) or
maximum entitlement whichever is less.

ii. In case of travel by hired car (AC or Non -AC), the bills must be produced
to claim the reimbursements.
iii. Employees of the level of Middle Management and above are entitled to
engage a car on a continuous basis as required during tour outside Head
Quarters. All others are entitled to engage the car on a point -to-point
basis.
iv. Employees shall record the mileage travelled, on the trip sheet.
v. In case more than 3 resources are travelling together, SUV or similar
vehicle may be hired on need basis. The claim for this will be done on
actuals

10. Travel Advance
i. All employees are entitled to claim a Business Travel Advance equal to
90% of the indicative travel expense calculated based on their eligibility
criteria
ii. Employees should submit their travel claims within 10 working days after
completing each tour.
iii. Employees shall not be eligible for any further Travel Advance if they have
not settled the account of their two previous business travels.
iv. Employees who have drawn Travel Advance and fail to perform the
approved Travel for any reason shall refund the advance drawn forthwith
to MyGov failing which penal interest shall be leviable on the advance
drawn. Similarly un -utilised portion of advance shall be remitted back to
MyGov on return from Travel within 10 working days and thereafter
interest shall be leviable on such un-utilised advance.

MyGov LEAVE POLICY

1. Objective

The objective of this policy is to ensure that resources are able to balance
personal and professional life without compromising business continuity and
discipline.

2. Scope

The policy is applicable to all resources at MyGov.

3. Guidelines

a) Leave entitlement and computation are linked to the calendar year i.e. from
January 1 to December 31.

b) Other than Maternity Leave, no leave can be claimed as a matter of right. It
should be planned in advance in consultation with the manager in a manner
that it does not impact the business adversely or dis rupt the functioning of
the Vertical.
c) Leave can be refused, revoked, curtailed by the Department/ Ministry based on
business exigencies.

d) Resources are eligible to avail only casual / sick leave during the probation and sick
leave during notice period.

e) A resource can avail the following types of leave based on the need and reason of
absence:

o Earned Leave (EL)
o Casual Leave (CL)

o Sick Leave (SL)

f) A resource can proceed for Earned leave only after approval by the concerned
Department official.

g) All resources are expected to apply for leave i.e. EL, SL, and CL etc.

h) Apart from the permitted Leaves, a List of Holidays for the Calendar Year is also
published by MyGov. These holidays are in addition to the permissible leaves.

4. Leave Benefits

(A) Earned Leave

Entitlement 15 days per year/prorated during the year of joining and separation.
Earned Leave cannot be availed in advance. EL has to be accumulated first
at the rate of 1.25 days per month of service before being availed.
Purpose May be used for personal reasons
Process Can be availed only with prior approval of the immediate manager.
HR must be notified of the approval. Clubbing of Intervening holidays
and weekends would be treated/counted towards leave.
For instance, in case of leaves availed on Friday and Monday, it will
be counted as 4 days leave. Intervening holidays will also be counted
as leave.
In case of leave availed on a Friday or Monday, it will be counted as
1 day leave.
Accumulation A maximum of 10 Earned leaves can be carried forward to the
next year by an employee. Total accumulation of EL on an
employee’s account is capped at 30 days. EL accumulation
above 30 days will be considered as lapsed.
Encashment Not eligible.
In case of separation accumulated EL can be adjusted against unserved
notice period, if any, with the approval of competent authority for
extreme situations and the residual EL, if any, will lapse. Residual Leave,
after such adjustment, will not be encashed on separation.

(B) Casual Leave

Entitlement 06 days per year – cannot be carried over or combined with any other
leave. Is prorated during the year of joining and separation
Purpose May be used for personal reasons
Process Can be availed with prior intimation preferably. Intervening holidays
and weekends are not treated / counted towards leave.
Encashment Not eligible
Accumulation No accumulation of CL is done.

(C) Sick Leave

Entitlement 06 days per year / prorated during the year of joining and separation
Purpose May be used for medical reasons
Process Can be availed for medical reasons. Intervening holidays and
weekends are not treated as leave. Leave availed beyond three days
requires a medical fitness certificate to be submitted.
Encashment Not Applicable
Accumulation Can be accumulated up to 25 days. All Sick Leave above 3 days will require
a medical certificate.

(D) Maternity Leave

Eligibility Provision of this leave are all governed by the Maternity Benefit conditions
provided in Chapter 6 of the Code on Social Security 2020 of the
Government of India. Employees are required to consult the Code for
further details. All female resources who have worked at least for a period
of 80 days or more in the twelve months preceding the date of expected
delivery are eligible for maternity leave. The leave entitlement for a woman
with one or no surviving children is 26 weeks, of which 8 weeks can be
taken prior to delivery. For a woman with two or more surviving children
maximum leave allowed is 12 weeks, of which 6 can be taken before
delivery. Under the Code leave benefits of 12 weeks are allowed to women
adopting a child below the age of 3 months or obtai ning one through
surrogacy. The Code also lays down leave entitlement in conditions of

miscarriage and other health emergencies during pregnancy which will
apply in case it is necessary.
Process Expectant mothers are to keep their Manager and HR informed about the
date of delivery and plan their leave before and after the date accordingly.
Encashment Maternity leave is a paid leave and encashment is not allowed
Accumulation Accumulation of Maternity Leave is not permitted.
In extraordinary circumstances MyGov may allow combining other leave
for which the employee is eligible with ML and to extend the duration with
prior approval of the competent authorit y provided the employee have
sufficient or required leave balance.

(E) Paternity Leave

Eligibility All male resources once in a fixed tenure up to a maximum of two
occasions during the total engagement period.
Paternity Leave is also admissible on valid adoption of a child below
the age of one year.
Entitlement Fifteen (15) working days
Purpose Paternity leave can be availed within one month of delivery.
Process Can be availed with prior approval of the immediate manager

HR must be notified of the approval.
Extension Not permitted
Encashment Not permitted
Accumulation Not permitted

(F) Half Day Leave

Half Day Leave When applying for a half day leave a resource is required to spend a
minimum of 4 business hours at office. Half day leave can be used from the
balance in the Casual and Sick Leave categories first and then from Earned
Leave. No separate entitlement in days is available for Half Day Leave.
